label: early original-phase first-occurrence of t/d/r/c/y/k in sequences starting with e/n/f/0/z/b
explanation: Almost entirely an original-phase unit (98% of mass), peaking at t=3-4 with t=2..6 covering 97% of mass; it never fires at t=0 and hardly fires at the delimiter or during copying. Within that window it prefers specific input tokens (t 6.7x, d 5x, r 4.3x, then c, y, k, digits 2/3), first occurrences of the token, and sequences whose first token is n/e (about 5x) or f/0/z/b. The largest activations are t/d/r at step 3-5 after an earlier o, in sequences beginning with e/n/f/0. The window alone has 3% precision. The token-by-first-token conjunction gives only about 0.4 F1 and about 0.53 mass recall, so the neuron seems to read a distributed combination of prefix identity that this predicate captures only in part.
